### What does this PR do?

Roadmap item 2 of [RFC #8324](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/8324), split from [integration preview #25](https://github.com/ISEEKYAN/verl/pull/25), **depends on [upstream #8438](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8438)**. This upstream draft targets `main`, so its current diff includes step 1. Review step 1 first; this branch will be rebased after it merges to leave only forward execution changes. [Fork preview #27](https://github.com/ISEEKYAN/verl/pull/27) shows the isolated step-2 diff against fork #26. Submitted at the author's request; human line review remains pending.

Replace the copied GPT forward with native output callbacks. Eager and fused paths share THD/BSHD preparation, context labels, CP metadata and output unpacking. Per-forward context is immutable; callbacks use the output layer's explicit TP group and preserve sequence-parallel gradient behavior. Convert Core's sequence-major hidden layout to batch-major token order before the fused kernel.

### Checklist Before Starting

- [x] Checked [open fused PRs](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+megatron+fused) and [RFC-linked PRs](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+8324+in%3Abody).
- [x] Title follows project format.

This is the structural migration from #25, not a competing implementation of #8029 (parameter synchronization), #7826 (MTP fused BSHD), #7499 (legacy missing labels) or #8031 (MTP head gradients). Native readiness is used when available; the helper from #8029 is reused once installed. Old Core with overlapping parameter gather and no readiness helper safely selects eager output. No new DDP bucket synchronization implementation is introduced. MTP/value-model fused exclusions remain unchanged; retained legacy MTP postprocessing (including zero-MTP references) is detected after compatibility setup and also stays eager; MTP/replay migration and recompute cleanup remain later slices.

### Test

- Slurm CPU with **official Core 0.19.2** (`core_v0.19.2`) and **official Core 0.21 main** (`b9d4e2b2`), without companion-fork source. Torch 2.13.0+cpu / Transformers 5.16.1. **80 passed, 1 skipped on each official Core version.**
- H100, Torch 2.11.0+cu130 / TE 2.15 image, official Core source: **2 passed on 0.19.2 and 2 passed on 0.21**. Actual BF16 Triton fused output agrees with an eager reference for log-probabilities, entropy, hidden gradients and tied/untied output-weight gradients.
- CPU coverage includes real Core `GPTModel.forward` callback execution, THD/BSHD eager-versus-callback value/gradient parity, native forward identity, per-call label context, explicit TP/SP contracts, backend setup, eager fallback, and existing MTP/DCP/replay/packing regressions.
- All-files pre-commit and `git diff --check` pass.

CPU command: `python -m pytest --noconftest --import-mode=importlib -q tests/models/test_model_forward_fused.py tests/utils/megatron/test_compat_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_megatron_mtp_dcp.py tests/utils/test_megatron_router_replay_dcp.py tests/utils/test_megatron_bshd_preprocess.py tests/workers/test_megatron_liger_fused_kernels_on_cpu.py`.

GPU command: `python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node=1 -m pytest --noconftest --import-mode=importlib -q tests/models/test_megatron_native_output_gpu.py`.

### API and Usage Example

Engine setup calls the shared compatibility boundary and receives whether native fused output is supported. Providers missing `output_processor` / `output_processor_context` keep their original forward and use eager execution. The old `patch_fused_forward` setup name remains an alias for callback configuration and no longer patches a method. Fused BSHD selects the same shared adapter as eager BSHD. Public model inputs and RL objectives are unchanged.

### Design & Code Changes

`model_forward_fused.py` loses the legacy copied forward and separate packing implementation. `model_forward.py` owns layouts and attaches per-forward packed labels to callback context. Core owns wrapper unwrapping, avoiding the old FSDP factory/type mismatch. The compatibility registry retires its legacy fused-forward entry. Existing MTP packed normalization metadata remains in place for the later MTP migration.

### Checklist Before Submitting

- [x] Read contribution guide and ran all-files pre-commit.
- [x] Documentation and CPU/GPU regressions.
- [ ] Human line review and full distributed model acceptance.

The H100 result is a real output-kernel smoke, not end-to-end model training or qualification of the new locked CUDA environment. TP>1, PP/VPP, full model throughput/memory, FP8/QAT and NPU/ROCm remain separate acceptance work. No Core/Bridge dependency pin changes or new Core/Bridge PRs are required for this slice. Prepared with Codex assistance.

+"""Actual BF16 Triton output kernel agrees with an eager vocabulary reference."""

+import os
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.distributed as dist
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from verl.models.mcore.model_forward_fused import FusedOutputProcessorContext, fused_output_processor
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="Requires CUDA fused output kernels")
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def tp_group():
+    torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ.get("LOCAL_RANK", "0")))
+    owned_group = not dist.is_initialized()
+    if owned_group:
+        dist.init_process_group("nccl")
+    assert dist.get_world_size() == 1, "This numerical smoke uses one vocabulary partition"
+    yield dist.group.WORLD
+    if owned_group:
+        dist.destroy_process_group()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tied", [False, True])
+def test_actual_fused_output_values_and_gradients(tp_group, tied):
+    torch.manual_seed(83)
+    hidden = torch.randn(4, 2, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
+    weight = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.randn(128, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.05)
+    labels = torch.randint(128, (2, 4), device="cuda")
+    result = fused_output_processor(
+        hidden_states=hidden,
+        output_layer=SimpleNamespace(weight=weight, tp_group=tp_group),
+        output_weight=weight if tied else None,
+        labels=labels,
+        context=FusedOutputProcessorContext(0.7),
+        config=SimpleNamespace(sequence_parallel=False, config_logger_dir=""),
+    )
+    logits = F.linear(hidden.transpose(0, 1).float(), weight.float()) / 0.7
+    logp = logits.log_softmax(-1)
+    expected_logp = logp.gather(-1, labels.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)
+    expected_entropy = -(logp.exp() * logp).sum(-1)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(result["log_probs"].float(), expected_logp, atol=2e-2, rtol=2e-2)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(result["entropy"].float(), expected_entropy, atol=2e-2, rtol=2e-2)
+    actual_grads = torch.autograd.grad(
+        result["log_probs"].mean() + 0.01 * result["entropy"].mean(), (hidden, weight), retain_graph=True
+    )
+    expected_grads = torch.autograd.grad(expected_logp.mean() + 0.01 * expected_entropy.mean(), (hidden, weight))
+    for actual, expected in zip(actual_grads, expected_grads, strict=True):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual.float(), expected.float(), atol=5e-4, rtol=5e-2)

+
+Eager and fused execution share `model_forward.py` for THD/BSHD packing, packed
+labels, dynamic-CP metadata and output unpacking. Fused output uses an immutable
+per-forward context and Core's output callback; it never replaces model `forward`.
+Sequence-parallel gathers use the output layer's TP group, with the existing
+backend-specific hidden-gradient reduction contract. The callback converts
+sequence-major hidden states to batch-major token order before the fused kernel.
